core.author: Vershawn Ashanti Young
core.title: Should Writers Use They Own English?
core.readingBoundary: Full essay; embedded teaching cards are brief excerpts and paraphrased reading guides, not the complete text.

biography.use: He/him and teaching/scholar identity; not additional invented positions.

objective: Answer an objection while advancing the claim
fiction: All encounters, characters other than Young, imagined dialogue and outcomes are invented. Only explicitly labelled excerpts reproduce the article. The bathroom/computer joke is user-requested fictional dialogue. Jordan is one fictional person, not a representative of all African American English speakers.
aiScope: Five trusted source cards, including Young’s first-person faculty statement and a fixed rubric. No claim to simulate consciousness or access to an unverified corpus. Supports revision without grades. Card references and plausible inferences are separated.
